function_question: How does nature move and store water without a pump?

opening.text: There was a girl called Hana whose class grew a row of bean plants on the sunny classroom windowsill.
Hana was the plant monitor. She watered the beans each morning and measured how much taller they had grown.
Their teacher sighed. "The school closes for two weeks of holiday, and I can't come in to water them." Hana looked at the plants. "Then we'll build them a plant sitter!"

card.problem: The plants will be alone for two weeks
card.goal: Keep a plant watered for 2 weeks
card.rules: No people, no pumps, no electricity

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: Two weeks alone
chapters.line: Hana wonders: how can a plant get a drink when nobody is there?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Hana needs a helper
chapters.line: A whole windowsill of plants needs two caring designers. Will you join Hana?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The nature heroes
chapters.line: You and Hana meet heroes that move and save water with no pump at all.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of the thin path
chapters.line: The heroes show how water can climb all by itself.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: The wick race

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: In the teacher's shoes
chapters.line: You imagine what the teacher says, thinks, does and feels.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan

chapters.label: Chapter 7

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Welcome back, beans

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Hana's class plants will be alone for two weeks of holiday, with nobody to water them. Can you help her? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some designers already have an idea for a plant that waters itself. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been moving water without pumps for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four water-wise heroes!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which wick will pull the coloured water up the highest? Don't drink the test water.
guide.sketch: Time to draw your plant sitter from the side, like a real garden engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your plant sitter and check the soil every day. How many days does it stay damp?
guide.retry_tip: Designers never stop at round 1. Change just ONE thing, like the wick or the water store, and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Hana's class plant sitters look after the windowsill every holiday, and the teacher can relax.

quick_check.question: A small plant drinks about 40 ml of water a day. How much water does it need for 14 days?
quick_check.right: Right! 40 × 14 = 560 ml. So a 1-litre bottle is a good size for your water store.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Multiply: 40 ml × 14 days. Try 40 × 10, then add 40 × 4.

clue_cards.name: Tree
clue_cards.trick: Millions of very thin tubes from roots to leaves.
clue_cards.does: Water creeps up the tubes, pulled along as it evaporates from the leaves.

clue_cards.name: Cactus
clue_cards.trick: Pleats that spread out as it fills with water.
clue_cards.does: It stores rainwater and uses it slowly through the dry months.

clue_cards.name: Moss
clue_cards.trick: Tiny leaves and stems full of spaces.
clue_cards.does: It soaks up many times its own weight in water and lets it go slowly.

clue_cards.name: Camel
clue_cards.trick: It drinks a huge amount at once, then loses very little.
clue_cards.does: Its nose catches moisture from its breath, so the water lasts.

match_groups.label: 🧽 A sponge that holds and lets go

predict.prompt: Pulls water up or stays dry? Predict first!

items.label: A cotton string dipped in water
The tip of a paper towel in a spill
A metal spoon standing in water

predict.explain: Cotton and paper are made of thin fibres with tiny gaps between them. Water sticks to the fibres and creeps along the gaps. A solid metal spoon has no tiny gaps, so the water can't climb.

lab.title: The wick race lab
lab.predict: Dip each wick in coloured water for 10 minutes. Which one will pull the water up the highest?
lab.measure: height the water climbs in 10 minutes (cm)

tool.name: Empathy Map
tool.intro: An Empathy Map helps you understand the person you're designing for. You fill in 4 boxes: what they Say, Think, Do and Feel. Today you'll learn all 4, and use them for Hana's teacher.

parts.name: Says
parts.what: Words the person says out loud.

parts.name: Thinks
parts.what: Thoughts they might keep to themselves.

parts.name: Does
parts.what: Things you can see them do.
parts.example: 🍱 Puts the lunchbox on top of the bag, very carefully.

parts.name: Feels
parts.example: 🍱 Hungry, grumpy and a little bit sad.
parts.starter: When the teacher thinks about the plants, they feel…
